parts:
I noticed that the GM-related tests toward the end of test-all take a
lot of RAM nowdays (like 4GB). Maybe the failures are due to that
getting maxed out? Or maybe those tests could be split into smaller
pieces?

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Stopping GM Tests on Jenkins build for a bit.
parts:
This one is a little different. It's a compiler related issue. The
models stopped building after refactoring.

Moving namespaces, changes to physical layout, and adding one header
file that includes others. Somewhere in there, it makes g++ on windows
fail without any intelligible error message. My mac can handle it
fine.

On a similar note, I can't get clang to use the precompiled header
without crashing. It complains about too many open files.

> I noticed that the GM-related tests toward the end of test-all take a
> lot of RAM nowdays (like 4GB). Maybe the failures are due to that
> getting maxed out? Or maybe those tests could be split into smaller
> pieces?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Stopping GM Tests on Jenkins build for a bit.
parts:
Who knew that compilation was an experimental
science?

- Bob

On 2/16/12 12:03 PM, Daniel Lee wrote:
> This one is a little different. It's a compiler related issue. The
> models stopped building after refactoring.
>
> Moving namespaces, changes to physical layout, and adding one header
> file that includes others. Somewhere in there, it makes g++ on windows
> fail without any intelligible error message. My mac can handle it
> fine.
>
> On a similar note, I can't get clang to use the precompiled header
> without crashing. It complains about too many open files.

Might some file somewhere not have a header
guard and be getting continually compiled?

The only namespace shift was for the models
prob_grad and prob_grad_ad, which moved to
their own namespace, stan::model?

This would turn off argument-dependent lookup
for variables that are in the stan::mcmc namespace
getting passed to functions in the models.

We should also do a thorough "using" review.
I'm still worried there may be order dependencies
in the compiles.

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Stopping GM Tests on Jenkins build for a bit.

I moved the order of the includes in the generated model and it worked.

I'm not going to think too hard about why, but if I do find the

I'm pretty sure this means that we have some
.hpp files that aren't including everything
they should, but rather relying on other files
to include it.

If we design our headers well, order of includes
shouldn't matter.

So we should definitely clean this up if we can
track it down. We should sit down and review
all the "using"s in the entire package.

- Bob
